issues.description: Title/branding mismatch between PR (compute_image_publicly_shared) and code (compute_image_not_publicly_shared) signals unreasoned naming discipline.
issues.detail: The PR description and class commentary describe a check named compute_image_publicly_shared, while the directory, metadata CheckID, class, and CHANGELOG entry use compute_image_not_publicly_shared. Names are part of the specification. Either the spec is wrong or the code is; the author has not stated which. REASONED code does not exhibit this inconsistency.

issues.description: Postcondition silently violated: on getIamPolicy failure, image is classified PASS rather than UNKNOWN.
issues.detail: When getIamPolicy raises (e.g. permission denied on image 3 in the fixture), the except branch logs and falls through, leaving publicly_shared=False. The check then reports PASS for an image whose policy was never read. The postcondition (PASS iff allAuthenticatedUsers absent) is false. This is DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE: try/except in place of a correct three-valued status.

issues.description: Bare `except Exception` swallows all errors including KeyError, TypeError, and programmer faults.
issues.detail: Both try blocks catch Exception with no narrowing. A malformed response missing the `name` key would be logged as if it were an API permission error and the loop would continue with corrupted state. The author has not stated which exceptions are anticipated and why the others are safe to ignore. UNREASONED error handling.

issues.description: Loop invariant for the IAM bindings scan is unstated; early break on first allAuthenticatedUsers is correct but unjustified in comments.
issues.detail: The inner loop's invariant is: publicly_shared is true iff some scanned binding contains allAuthenticatedUsers. The author asserts this implicitly. A one-line invariant comment, plus the role being ignored (any role granted to allAuthenticatedUsers is the risk), would make the reasoning auditable rather than inferred.

issues.description: Tests demonstrate presence of the happy path, not absence of bugs; the IAM-policy-failure case is never asserted at check level.
issues.detail: Fixture image 3 triggers an exception in getIamPolicy and the service test merely asserts publicly_shared is False. No test asserts what the check reports when IAM is unreadable. TESTED-NOT-PROVED: the most security-relevant failure mode (unknown policy reported as PASS) is the one path not exercised end-to-end.

issues.description: Image listing does not distinguish custom from public/marketplace images; specification claims it does.
issues.detail: The PR text states the check evaluates 'custom images', but images().list(project=project_id) on a user project returns whatever that project owns; no filter (e.g. family, source, deprecated.state) is applied. If the precondition is 'custom images only', the code does not establish it. State the precondition or enforce it.

review.summary: The check is small, structured, and largely follows the surrounding GCP service idioms, but it is not REASONED at the level the security claim demands. The author has not stated preconditions (what is a "custom image"?), postconditions (what does PASS mean when the IAM policy could not be read?), or invariants for the bindings scan. The most consequential defect is DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE: a getIamPolicy failure silently yields PASS, and the tests never exercise that path at the check layer. Naming is inconsistent between PR text and code, which is a small flag for a larger discipline problem. Fix the unknown-policy postcondition, narrow exception handling, and the rest is acceptable.
